record.paper_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
record.original_question: How can the theoretical uncertainty in deep inelastic scattering be improved beyond the current practice of varying the renormalization and factorization scales within conventional brackets, given that the perturbative expression still contains higher-twist corrections and the source states that it is not clear how to do any better?

Not currently close to this ideal situation, the practice consists in defining a “theoretical uncertainty” as the range of results in the brackets µR/2 < µF < 2 µR; µF /2 < µR < 2 µF . It is not clear how to do any better.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In perturbative QCD applied to deep inelastic scattering (DIS), an observable such as a structure function is computed as a truncated expansion in the strong coupling $\alpha_s(\mu_R)$ together with parton distribution functions evolved at a factorization scale $\mu_F$, plus power-suppressed higher-twist corrections of the form $\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}^2/Q^2)$ that are not captured by the perturbative series. The standard prescription for assigning a "theoretical uncertainty" to a fixed-order prediction is to take the envelope of results obtained as $(\mu_R,\mu_F)$ vary over the conventional brackets
$$\mu_R/2 \le \mu_F \le 2\mu_R, \qquad \mu_F/2 \le \mu_R \le 2\mu_F,$$
about a central choice $\mu_R=\mu_F=Q$. This procedure has no rigorous statistical interpretation, ignores higher-twist contributions, and depends on an arbitrary factor of two.

Problem. Devise a principled, quantitatively reliable method for estimating the theoretical uncertainty of a perturbative DIS prediction that improves upon the standard scale-variation envelope. Specifically, formulate a scheme that
(i) provides an estimator of the uncertainty due to missing higher orders in $\alpha_s$ with a defensible probabilistic or otherwise rigorous interpretation,
(ii) accounts in a controlled way for unknown higher-twist (power-suppressed) corrections to the structure functions, and
(iii) yields uncertainty bands that, in the limit of arbitrarily many computed perturbative orders, converge to the true theoretical error.
Either construct such a method and prove it satisfies (i)–(iii), or demonstrate that no such improvement over the conventional bracket prescription is possible without additional nonperturbative input.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (NNPDF and collaborators, 2019–2024) has developed a "theory covariance matrix" approach using correlated renormalization/factorization scale variations to estimate missing-higher-order uncertainties (MHOUs) in PDF fits and DIS predictions, providing a more systematic Bayesian-flavored framework than naive bracket variation. However, no fully rigorous method that simultaneously handles higher-twist (power-suppressed) corrections has been established; treatment of nonperturbative power corrections remains process-dependent and incomplete. The problem is therefore partially addressed but not closed.

status_evidence.title: Parton distributions with theory uncertainties: general formalism and first phenomenological studies
status_evidence.snippet: Renormalization and factorization scale variations are used as a means to estimate missing higher order uncertainties (MHOUs) consistently in deep inelastic and hadronic processes via a theory covariance matrix.
status_evidence.claim: A systematic theory covariance matrix framework improves on naive scale-variation envelopes for DIS MHOUs.

status_evidence.title: Determination of theory uncertainties from missing higher orders on NNLO parton distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work focuses on the treatment of MHOUs and their full correlations through a theory covariance matrix determined by scale variation.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024 the MHOU covariance approach is still being refined; higher-twist treatment is not part of the formalism.

status_evidence.title: On the consistent use of scale variations in PDF fits and predictions
status_evidence.snippet: Independent scale variations capture MHOUs in DGLAP evolution and partonic cross sections separately.
status_evidence.claim: Independent factorization/renormalization variations refine but do not eliminate the ambiguity of the bracket prescription.
